speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: When the pandemic first broke out, some thought it might be all over after a year.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We are dealing with a very tricky virus.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Even countries which kept their borders tight like China and Australia are seeing outbreaks of new clusters linked to this variant.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The Delta variant is fast becoming the world’s dominant strain of SARS-CoV-2.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It has spread throughout Asia and is now making its way to countries around the world.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: For example, Members would have read reports of how new infections are surging across the African continent because of the Delta variant.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Some countries that started relaxing their measures are also seeing new infections due to this strain.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But in places where the vaccination rates are not high enough, especially amongst the elderly population, the increase in infections may unfortunately lead to higher hospitalisation, ICU admissions and eventually fatalities.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The world is unlikely to reach a point where enough people are immune to stop the virus’ spread before the emergence of new variants.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Delta may not be the worst variant of this virus.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: I shudder to think what the Omega variant would look like.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We must be prepared to see new strains that are more transmissible, vaccine-resistant and even able to evade current diagnostic tests.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: For Singapore, we can take heart that we are in a much better position to deal with the pandemic now, than at the start.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We have more robust public health defences, including testing and contact tracing capabilities, which have enabled us to quickly detect and contain the spread of new clusters.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We have procured enough mRNA vaccines as part of our national programme and are now able to offer these vaccines to all eligible persons in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And to deal with the latest round of outbreaks, we decided there was no need to go into an economy-wide circuit breaker like what we had done last year.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We introduced measures aimed at reducing transmission risks in indoor settings where people do not have their masks on and where there is a higher chance of large clusters forming.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: These included F&B dining-in, gyms and fitness centres, as well as live arts and cultural performances.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In line with this calibrated approach during the Heightened Alert, we have targeted our support measures to help businesses and individuals most impacted by the tightened restrictions.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The details of the support measures have been announced previously.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, let me just provide a quick summary.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: First, we enhanced the Jobs Support Scheme, or JSS, to help enterprises retain local workers.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: From 16 May to 11 July, we provided different levels of JSS enhancements based on the impact of our measures on various sectors.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We provided 50% JSS support for sectors which had to suspend all or most of their operations.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: These included F&B, gyms, fitness studios, as well as performing arts organisations and arts education centres.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We also enhanced support to 30% for sectors that were not required to suspend operations but were, nonetheless, significantly impacted by the reduced footfall.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: These included the retail sector, cinemas, museums, art galleries, historical sites, indoor playgrounds and other family entertainment centres.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: To ease businesses back towards reopening, we will taper JSS support to 10% for two weeks from 12 July.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Second, we helped businesses with their cash flow by providing relief for rental costs.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We provided two months of rental waiver for hawkers in Government-owned premises.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: To support smaller businesses, including those in the heartlands, we extended rental support for Small and Medium Enterprises, or SMEs, and eligible non-profit organisations through one month of rental waiver for tenants of Government-owned commercial properties and half a month of cash payout for those who are end-tenants and owner-occupiers of qualifying private commercial properties.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Third, we helped individuals impacted by the safe management measures.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We supported taxi and private hire car drivers through the COVID-19 Driver Relief Fund.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The coverage for this CRG-T scheme extends to end-July.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In coming up with this package, we consulted closely with workers, union leaders and business leaders to hear their concerns and challenges and I thank them for their understanding and close cooperation as we navigate this crisis together.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We sized the package based on what we assessed to be appropriate to meet the needs of businesses and individuals during this period.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: As mentioned earlier, most parts of our economy continued to operate over the past two months.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It was not the same as the circuit breaker last year where many activities were curtailed and literally the whole economy was shut down.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In fact, many individuals and businesses have learnt to adapt and pivot to new ways of working and doing business, allowing them to keep going in the face of tightened restrictions.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We are also building on a strong base of support measures announced earlier this year in Budget 2021 and which are still in place.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: For example, we have the Jobs Growth Incentive and other measures in the SGUnited Jobs and Skills Package to facilitate workers moving to jobs in growth areas.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We also have measures to foster innovation, help businesses adopt new technologies and build deep digital capabilities and we continue to have various assistance schemes for individuals and households, including the GST Vouchers, CDC Vouchers and the COVID-19 Recovery Grant.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Drawing on past reserves is a major move.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Our economy shrank by 5.4%, the largest fall since Independence.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Our resident unemployment rate rose to nearly 5%.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: At the start of this financial year, because we were starting out on a new term, we had to draw on past reserves again to finance the continuing COVID-related measures in the Budget.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We are not in the same situation this time.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Our economy is recovering; our employment situation is steadily improving.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: On the COVID-19 front, we have improved testing and tracing capabilities and we can now control the infection with more targeted restrictions.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We have also made good progress on vaccinations.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Almost 40% of our population has been fully vaccinated and we are going as fast as we can with nearly 80,000 doses being administered every day.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will not hesitate to use the full measure of our fiscal firepower to protect the lives and livelihoods of Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But we also need to be careful about the state of our public finances and ensure they are sustainable for the future.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In many countries, COVID-19 has led to massive increases in debt levels, which have not been seen since the end of the Second World War.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Not many people are paying attention to how all of this debt will be serviced.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: They may look affordable now, but will not be so once interest rates increase to more normal levels.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The day of reckoning will come and the burden will surely fall on the young and future generations.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We are one of the very few exceptions to this trend of rising public debt around the world.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We are very fortunate to be where we are today, thanks to the foresight and fiscal prudence of our forefathers.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: When the Reserves Protection Framework was introduced in 1991, no one could have foreseen that a pandemic of this magnitude would hit us one day.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It is an amount which we are not likely to be able to put back anytime soon, if at all.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Our expenditure in FY2020 was the highest ever in the history of our country; and this unprecedented fiscal response has also led to the largest Budget deficit in Singapore’s history.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Now that things are better, we should refrain from drawing further on past reserves.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Instead, we will fund the support measures using resources that were approved in this year’s Budget.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: There are two projects that meet the criteria for financing under SINGA:  the Deep Tunnel Sewerage System and the North-South Corridor.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We had set aside funds for these two projects in Budget 2021, before SINGA was passed.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: With SINGA, we will borrow for these projects and capitalise their development expenditure from the fourth quarter of this year.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The amount that was originally budgeted to finance these two projects can now be reallocated to fund this support package.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This is a one-off adjustment, because SINGA was passed after we started the financial year.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Going forward, the amounts that will be capitalised under SINGA will be incorporated as part of future annual Budget Estimates and, so, we will not have such reallocation space in future.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It does not mean we are cancelling the projects.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We still want to do the projects and we will have to catch up on our development schedules as the situation stabilises.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, the delayed expenditure will still need to be incurred in future financial years.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Even before the crisis, we have been careful to ensure a fair tax regime for everyone.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Our overall income tax revenue, both corporate and personal, as a percentage of GDP, is low, at only around 6%, about half of the OECD average of 12%.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: For individuals, we layer on a progressive system of transfers that provides more help for those in greater need.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And as we have shared in this House before, the bottom 20% of households by income, for example, receive around $4 of benefits for every dollar of tax they contribute.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We also have a competitive tax regime for companies, particularly our SMEs, as they are the backbone of our economy.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: While there is a global movement to change corporate tax rules, which we discussed at length just now, these changes are only applicable to a select group of global companies and not to smaller enterprises.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, our SMEs in Singapore can continue to enjoy low taxes.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Our SMEs, or those with turnover of up to $100 million, comprise more than 95% of active companies in Singapore, but they contribute less than a third of our corporate income tax revenue – 95% versus one-third.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In fact, more than 50% of such companies do not pay any corporate tax at all.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Besides taxes, we recognise that SMEs are concerned with business costs, like rental, labour and utilities.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We do not directly offset such costs in normal times but, instead, provide a wide range of schemes to help them improve productivity and build new capabilities.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, from 2015 to 2019, before COVID-19, about 70% of Government grant disbursements went to SMEs.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: During times of crises, we recognise that lower-income households and SMEs face bigger challenges.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: That is why we have designed our interventions to benefit them the most.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In particular, our COVID-19 support packages provide more help for SMEs.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: About 90% of the benefits from the corporate income tax rebate in the Year of Assessment 2020 went to SMEs.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: For many SMEs, access to credit is a critical lifeline to tide them through this crisis.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: That is why we have supported over $22 billion worth of loans to over 25,000 enterprises through Enterprise Singapore’s financing schemes since the start of 2020.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) will also extend the MAS Singapore Dollar Facility for Enterprise Singapore Loans accordingly.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: I encourage businesses to make use of this extension and other available schemes to ready themselves for the new normal.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Many of our SMEs have already seized the opportunity to build new capabilities and future-proof their businesses.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Take the example of Slake, which started out in 2014 as a humble neighbourhood bistro in Siglap.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In 2017, even before the pandemic, Slake pivoted to online ordering to reach more customers by taking up the Productivity Solutions Grant.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: These investments paid off during the Circuit Breaker last year.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Since then, Slake has doubled down on their efforts to go digital.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It took up the Enterprise Development Grant to develop a virtual brand for new revenue streams, tapped on the Food Delivery Booster Package.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It recently also expanded its social media marketing and is now well-positioned for growth opportunities during this period and beyond.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: (In Mandarin):   In May this year, the Government tightened the restrictions and provided a series of support measures to the most affected individuals, workers and firms.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: When coming up with these measures, I am especially mindful of our SMEs' situation.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: However, they tend to have less resources due to their size.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: SMEs also tend to require more assistance when dealing with a crisis.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This is why we tend to tilt our policies towards SMEs by providing more support to them.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: For example, our SMEs enjoy low taxes in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: More than 50% of our SMEs do not pay any corporate income tax at all.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In addition, although SMEs comprise more than 95% of local companies, they contribute less than one-third of our total corporate income tax revenue.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The Government has paid out a total of $26.7 billion under the Jobs Support Scheme (JSS) to date and about two thirds of which went to SMEs.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Since the start of 2020 till today, Enterprise Singapore's financing schemes have supported more than 25,000 enterprises with over $22 billion worth of loans, and 99% of the recipients of the loans were SMEs.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Beyond this support, the Government will continue to support our businesses to digitalise and innovate to prepare them for recovery and growth post-COVID-19.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: (In English): Mr Speaker, looking ahead, the global economic outlook continues to be highly uncertain as it depends critically on the path of the pandemic.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: On the upside, the US is picking up strongly while the EU is showing the beginnings of a strong recovery.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: A faster-than-anticipated global vaccine rollout and effective pandemic containment could boost growth prospects.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: On the other hand, there are many downside risks, including the threat of new waves of infections, which could force a return to lockdowns in some jurisdictions and a slower timeline for the reopening of borders.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: As a small open economy, Singapore's outlook depends crucially on these external developments.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The uncertainty surrounding our economic outlook is, therefore, larger than usual.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But the recovery will be uneven across sectors.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The outward-oriented sectors which account for about 70% of our economy are projected to benefit from the pick-up in external demand.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The construction, marine and offshore engineering sectors are not short of projects but they face a severe manpower crunch due to the COVID-19 restrictions.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We have provided Foreign Worker Levy rebates to cushion the impact and other support measures to help these companies adapt and resume work safely.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But these cannot make up for the shortfall of workers.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, as we reopen our borders and allow more workers to come in, we expect the outlook for these industries to improve.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Likewise, domestic consumer-facing sectors like retail and F&B can expect to recover as we progressively ease our restrictions and allow larger groups to gather.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But the recovery will be more gradual in some of the hard-hit sectors like aviation and tourism-related industries because it will take a longer time for international air travel volumes to return to pre-COVID-19 levels.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, there might be some consolidation in these industries.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We, the Government, will do our part to reskill the affected workers and help them transition to other growing sectors that need manpower.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: One important part of the recovery process is the reopening of our borders.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It is, in fact, an existential issue for Singapore because we survive and thrive on our ability to connect businesses and people to the region and the world.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: There has been feedback from the business and investment community that Singapore might lose out to other hubs that are moving more aggressively to reopen their borders.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: While we will not be able to prevent occasional imported infections, a high vaccination rate and our public health defences will prevent major outbreaks.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Beyond the immediate term, we are investing in new capabilities and building ourselves up strongly for the future.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We are accelerating our automation and digitalisation efforts to help our businesses, especially SMEs, improve their productivity and transcend the limitations of our size and geography.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We are intensifying our efforts in SkillsFuture to equip our local workforce with deep skills and to power our next bound of growth with a strong Singaporean Core.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We are creating new investments and jobs in the green economy and strengthening our position as a regional centre for green finance.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We are investing in R&D to be at the forefront of new technological revolutions and to spur more innovative startups and enterprises.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Through all of these efforts, we will emerge from this crisis as a smarter and greener economy and a more innovative and inclusive nation.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The foundations for all these have been laid in previous Budgets under Deputy Prime Minister Heng.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We also convened the Emerging Stronger Task force, co-chaired by Minister Desmond Lee and Group CEO of PSA International Mr Tan Chong Meng, which has set out many useful recommendations to better position Singapore for future growth.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will double down on these efforts and develop new initiatives over the coming months to accelerate our progress.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: To achieve these goals, we will need strong partnerships across the community, private and public sectors.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Our experience throughout this pandemic has shown that we are stronger and more effective when we are united and when we work together.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: To conclude, Sir, I know that there is a deep longing in all our hearts to go back to how things were before the pandemic: to gather freely with our family and friends; to be able to travel freely for business and leisure; to be able to participate in religious activities and enjoy entertainment and sports events like football, although you can watch the European Championship (Euros) now on television; to go about our daily lives without masks.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: For many people, such a way of life can seem like a lifetime ago and they feel a sense of helplessness, not knowing when normalcy will return, if at all.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We see promising signs from countries that are ahead of us in vaccinations.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Its vaccination rate is amongst the highest in the world – about 60% of its population has been fully vaccinated with the Pfizer-BioNTech vaccine.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It has opened up most of its economy, relaxed many of its measures.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It is an ambitious target but we are making steady progress towards it.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: With high vaccination rates, we will be able reopen our economy safely.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will then ease the safe distancing rules progressively, especially for vaccinated persons, and we can look forward to larger gatherings, concerts, performances, sporting events and, eventually, to travel again.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We have been running this marathon together for some time.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But we are seeing light at the end of the tunnel.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Throughout the darkest moments of this pandemic, we have seen the Singapore spirit shine brightly.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, let us move forward with renewed confidence about the future because we will overcome this crisis together and we will emerge as a better, stronger and more united Singapore.
